plan.goal: Three outcomes, in one pass over the login clock (files/quickshell/greeter) and its workbench (packages/nixie): 1. Quality and performance: land the review findings (idle timers that never stop, strike-all on any minute change, shader UB/NaN edges, 208-248 texture taps/pixel without per-tube bounds, whole-window 4K repaint per shimmer tick) behind a quality tier and a shimmer token that default to today's picture. 2. Settings: expose the knobs a human wants as theme tokens (nixie<CamelCase>), with defaults equal to the current behaviour and documented ranges the menu must respect. 3. Menu: a live settings menu built from reusable widget components (sliders, colour fields, toggles, choices, sections, presets), mounted in the tube lab and the login preview, applying values to the running shader on the fly, with Save (user theme part), Reset and Export. The real login screen gains nothing interactive; it stays a lock surface. No system switch, no commit: the plan leaves a reviewed, verified working tree plus this document updated with results.

task.title: True 3D camera: world-space orbit and cursor follow

brief.TASK: The owner rejects the current camera as a 2D cheat: yaw shifts and narrows the numerals in screen space while the envelope keeps its head-on silhouette, so nothing reads as solid. Replace it with a real 3D camera: a world-space view transform (yaw + pitch + finite distance) generating a ray per pixel against the tube's actual 3D geometry (cylinder + shoulder + dome + pip, the cathode plane at its real depth, mesh and stack in their real places), so silhouette, internal parallax and glass reflections all respond correctly. The glass keeps its current physics (dispersion, wall reflection, absorption) but through the real camera; digits are evaluated where the refracted ray crosses the cathode plane. Cursor follow: effective yaw/pitch = base token + pointer offset (clamped to nixieCameraRange, smoothed) computed in QML and passed through pView as (yaw, distance, pitch, 0).

task.verification: All A1-A10 with raw output in /tmp; the report carries numbers, not adjectives.

risks.risk: The sandbox cannot open /dev/dri (llvmpipe in both nixie and qs), so absolute performance numbers are software-rendering numbers. Mitigation: relative before/after in the same environment, structural facts (timers, taps), and the caveat stated in every report.

Menu Save strips JSONC comments in the user's greeter.jsonc copy. Mitigation: user copy is machine state by contract; repo copy stays commented; repo save-back goes through the comment-preserving helper only; Save is atomic and parse-checked; documented.
Parallel writers conflict. Mitigation: strict file ownership (I3), no repo-wide formatters until P5, single writer on nixie.frag.
qmllint may not resolve the new module until its qmldir is picked up; the lint script scans qmldir files. Mitigation: P2 ships qmldir with the first edit and runs the lint.
Preview windows disturb the owner's session. Mitigation: move to special:nixie and kill after capture; short runs.

The idle fix changes visible timing (only the tube whose digit changed restrikes; shimmer at the token rate). Mitigation: A4 parity plus an explicit note in the report on the intended behaviour change.

Copy-once theme drift (runtime part already missing nixieTubeMargin) can make the menu's values diverge from the repo. Mitigation: P1 copies+touches and verifies; P5 applies repo values explicitly via the helper; A6 checks the round-trip.
Default quality tier change can alter the look. Mitigation: A4b gates it on numbers; otherwise default stays full.

The 3D camera is a rewrite of the shader's view path and can regress the accepted look. Mitigation: parity gate at yaw=pitch=0 (A4), numeric silhouette criterion (A11), P3 tiers re-measured (A8), single shader writer, P5 acceptance before any report; if parity cannot be restored after 2-3 iterations, revert to the P3 state and report the blocker instead of shipping a worse lamp.

handoff.order: P0 (done) -> in parallel [P1, P3, P4] -> P2 (needs P1's API and the camera tokens) -> P6 (after P1+P3; shader single writer) -> P5.
handoff.rules: Each subagent gets its task brief verbatim plus owns, MUST_DO/MUST_NOT_DO and verification; it works in the shared /etc/nixos tree, touches only its owns, does not commit, and returns: files changed, exact commands with raw result tails, numbers, and anything it could not verify. No narrative progress; the artifact is the report. If blocked, stop and report instead of widening scope.
handoff.commit_style: When the owner commits: bracketed scope, English imperative subject, e.g. "[greeter] ..." or "[dev/pkgs] ..."; body may be Russian.
